He can play at both the [[small forward]] and [[power forward]] positions. Nichols played [[college basketball]] with the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse Orange men's basketball team]], and has been a member of the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], [[Chicago Bulls]], and [[New York Knicks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). ==High school career== Nichols was coached by Mike Hart at [[St. Andrew's School (Rhode Island)|St. Andrew's High School]], where he helped his club to a 28–8 record and won the New England Prep School Athletic Conference title, tallying 15 points and 13 rebounds in the championship game against Lawrence Academy. His senior year, he averaged 18.6 points and 8.9 rebounds a game. He was a three-time Street & Smith's Magazine Honorable Mention All-American, a 2003 third-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]], the 2003 Rhode Island Gatorade Player of the Year, and the EA Sports Roundball Game All-American.{{cite web |title=Demetris Nichols Profile |url=http://www.suathletics.com/roster.asp?playerid=1455&sport=176&roster=194&path=mbasket |work=SUAthletics.com |access-date=2007-08-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927191148/http://www.suathletics.com/roster.asp?playerid=1455&sport=176&roster=194&path=mbasket |archive-date=2007-09-27 |url-status=dead }} He was rated 50th overall and 14th among small forwards by [[ESPN.com]]. He was successfully recruited by [[Syracuse University]].[https://assets.espn.go.com/recruiting/s/kruseondenic.html Recruiting priorities are changing] ==College career== Nichols appeared in 26 games for the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Orange]] during his freshman year, starting 15 of them. His best performance of the season was a seven-rebound and team-leading 17-point performance against Providence.[https://web.archive.org/web/20160915050806/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=240382507 Friars' first win at SU in seven tries] He also scored 10 points against BYU[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/playbyplay?gameId=244000035 Brigham Young vs. Syracuse - Play by Play - March 18, 2004] and nine points against Maryland in the NCAA Tournament,[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=244000037 Syracuse vs. Maryland - Box score - March 20, 2004] in which Syracuse advanced to the Sweet 16.[https://web.archive.org/web/20160915050810/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=244000037 Warrick's 26 carries 'Cuse to Sweet 16] In his sophomore year, Nichols would start the first eight games of the season before he was forced out of the lineup with a back injury.[https://web.archive.org/web/20160915034803/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=243630183 Syracuse has never lost to Albany] - "Demetris Nichols gave the Orange a big boost with 10 points after missing three games with a sore back" He would play in 27 games that season, averaging 3.9 points and 2.1 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=Demetris Nichols Prospect Profile |url=http://www.nba.com/draft2007/profiles/DemetrisNichols.html |work=NBA.com |access-date=2007-08-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160329081714/http://www.nba.com/draft2007/profiles/DemetrisNichols.html |archive-date=2016-03-29 |url-status=dead }} Nichols posted the sixth-best scoring average improvement in Syracuse history, going from 3.9 points per game as a sophomore to 13.3 points per game in 2005–06 in his junior year. He ranked second on the team in scoring and third in rebounding (5.8 rebounds per game). Nichols scored a season-high 28 points against [[University of Connecticut|Connecticut]][https://web.archive.org/web/20160915014736/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=260160183 Huskies put up road block, halt Orange's 12-game win streak] and averaged 13.0 points and 4.8 rebounds in the Big East Tournament. Nichols' senior season proved to be his best one at Syracuse, as he was a unanimous selection for the All-Big East First Team. He was also a NABC and USBWA All-District First Team selection after leading the Big East in scoring (18.9 points per game) and finished third in conference play (17.9 points per game). He also set a Syracuse record in Big East games with a career-high 37 points, including seven three-pointers, to go along with 10 rebounds against St. John's.[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=270212599 St. John's 64, Syracuse 60 - Box score - January 21, 2007] In March 2007, Nichols was elected to participate in the 19th Annual State Farm College Three-Point Championship. He finished second to [[Aaron Brooks (basketball)|Aaron Brooks]]. Nichols finished his Syracuse career tied for 28th in career scoring (1,344), third in three-point goals (205), fourth in three-point field goals attempted (573) and 10th in three-point field goal percentage (.358). ==Professional career== Nichols was taken in the second round (53rd overall) by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in the [[2007 NBA draft]], but immediately traded to the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for the Knicks' [[2008 NBA draft|2008 second round draft]] choice.{{cite web |title=Knicks deal for Nichols |first=Mike |last=Waters |date=2007-06-30 |url=http://www.syracuse.com/articles/sports/index.ssf?/base/sports-0/118319442561580.xml&coll=1 |work=Syracuse.com |access-date=2007-08-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071011102958/http://www.syracuse.com/articles/sports/index.ssf?%2Fbase%2Fsports-0%2F118319442561580.xml&coll=1 |archive-date=2007-10-11 |url-status=dead }} Nichols participated in the July 2007 [[NBA Summer League|Las Vegas Summer League]] with the Knicks and averaged 15.6 points on 53 percent shooting, including 23 points in the final game against the [[Denver Nuggets]]. He was second on the team in scoring as the Knicks went a perfect 5–0.{{cite web |title=Running the Table, Vegas Style |first=Dennis |last=D’Agostino |date=2007-07-15 |url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/news/nykveg_070716_summerleague.html |work=NBA.com |access-date=2007-08-25}} Following the summer league, Nichols fired his agent after the Knicks were attempting to work out a deal to send Nichols to Europe for the 2007–08 season. Originally, the Knicks had wanted Nichols to play in Italy because they had 17 contracts and only 15 roster spots. When Nichols heard of the arrangement, he fired then-agent [[Bill Duffy (basketball)|Bill Duffy]] in favor of Bill Neff and refused the Knicks' request. On October 1, Nichols was signed to the Knicks roster along with four other newcomers.{{cite news |title=Knicks Add Rookie Guard |first=Howard |last=Beck |date=2007-10-01 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/10/01/sports/basketball/01sportsbriefs-knicks.html?adxnnl=1&adxnnlx=1191298647-UZ6OxiPSCTDfd1VBubq96Q |work=New York Times |access-date=2007-10-01}} However, he was subsequently released by the Knicks on October 25, as the team needed to cut down its roster to 15 players.{{cite news|title=Knicks waive guards Jordan, Nichols, Russell|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=nba&id=3078717|access-date=July 24, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|date=October 25, 2007}} Then on October 29, he was signed by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] to fill the 15th spot on their opening day roster. Nichols sat on the bench for the first month of his time with the Cavaliers, but saw his first action on November 28, scoring 2 points in 8 minutes of playing time.[https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/boxscore;_ylt=AgzRV_OsyblmyAmXqXVWgPWQvLYF?gid=2007112808 NBA - Cleveland Cavaliers/Detroit Pistons Box Score Wednesday November 28, 2007 - Yahoo! Sports]{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} On December 5, 2007, Nichols was waived to clear roster space after the Cavs re-signed [[Anderson Varejão]] to end a contract dispute.[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3142432 Varejao can opt out of new Cavs deal after second season] Updated December 5, 2007 He was subsequently claimed by the [[Chicago Bulls]] and assigned to the [[Iowa Energy]] of the [[NBA G League|D-League]].{{cite web |title = Bulls Assign Nichols to D-League |date = 2007-12-18 |url = http://www.realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/49804/20071218/bulls_assign_nichols_to_d_league/ |work = RealGM |access-date = 2007-12-29 |url-status = dead |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20071220184859/http://www.realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/49804/20071218/bulls_assign_nichols_to_d_league/ |archive-date = 2007-12-20 }} After averaging 19.3 points per game in 14 appearances in the D-League, he was recalled to Chicago.
